Welcome & Background
About the Department

Welcome from the Head of Department

Welcome to the Department of Animal and Environmental Biology at Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko. The programme explores animal life and the relationships between organisms and their environment, combining classroom learning with laboratory and field-based study.

General overview:
The department was established as one of the university's foundation departments in 1999. The university's programme description highlights environmental processes, biodiversity, conservation, pollution control, sustainable food production and aquatic living resources. The department's history notes that it was renamed from Environmental Biology and Fisheries to Animal and Environmental Biology in 2015.

Areas of specialization include:
Fish Biology and Production, Genetics and Molecular Biology, Parasitology, Ecology, and Environmental Studies.

📍 View Department Location · Link coming soon
Official department page:
AAUA Animal and Environmental Biology
.

Programme Philosophy & Objectives
What the Programme Aims to Develop

Philosophy

To provide a sound understanding of traditional and modern zoology concepts, meet societal needs, and equip students with practical skills relevant to animal biology and environmental study.

Objectives

Develop understanding of animal biology, ecosystems and biological organisms.

Build subject-specific and transferable skills for fisheries, disease control, laboratories, teaching and forensic-related work.

Provide a foundation for postgraduate study and professional careers.

Enable students to apply scientific knowledge to practical problems and to design, conduct and interpret research.

Build interest in zoology across levels of biological organization and in modern molecular techniques.

Strengthen communication, presentation and lifelong-learning skills.

Develop critical thinking, computational and numerical skills.

Programme Offered & Duration
Degree Programmes

The university website lists Environmental Biology and Fisheries; the supplied departmental information also names Animal and Environmental Biology. The exact award title may depend on the applicable curriculum version.

🎓

B.Sc. Animal and Environmental Biology

Programme title provided in the department information supplied for this page.

⏱️

Duration

UTME: minimum of four years (eight semesters). Direct Entry: minimum of three years (six semesters), according to the official department page.

🐟

Study areas

Animal biology, ecology, fisheries, parasitology, genetics, environmental studies and related laboratory and field techniques.

Admission
Admission Requirements

UTME Entry Requirements

Five relevant O'Level credit passes, including English Language, Mathematics, Biology and Chemistry, plus one other relevant science subject (preferably Physics).

UTME subject combination supplied: English Language (compulsory), Biology, Chemistry, and Physics or Mathematics.

An acceptable UTME result is required for 100-Level entry.

Confirm current-year eligibility and subject combinations with the official AAUA/JAMB admission requirements before applying.

Direct Entry

The supplied programme document states five relevant SSC-equivalent credit passes, with two at Advanced Level. The following additional qualifications were also supplied and should be checked against the current AAUA admission notice:

ND/NID: minimum Upper Credit

HND: minimum Lower Credit

NCE: minimum 8 points

JUPEB: minimum 6 points

First degree: Second Class Lower (2:2) or higher

A-Levels: passes in two relevant subjects, subject to programme rules

Applicants must complete JAMB Direct Entry registration and AAUA screening when the respective portals open, and submit the required results and certificates.

Examination, Grading and Degree Classification

Examination System

Each course is examined at the end of the semester in which it is offered.

Continuous assessment may include tests, practicals, written assignments and other accepted methods.

Each course is scored out of 100%; continuous assessment contributes 30%.

Introduction & General Background
Department of Agribusiness

The B.Sc. Agribusiness programme equips students with the knowledge, skills and entrepreneurial mindset needed to address global food-security challenges and the changing demands of the agricultural sector.

Aligned with Nigeria’s National Policy on Agriculture, the programme combines theoretical knowledge with practical experience to develop professionals who can promote sustainable agricultural practices, increase food production, support economic diversification, strengthen agricultural supply chains, create employment and improve national self-sufficiency and resilience.

📍 View Faculty Location ↗

Programme Philosophy & Objectives
What the Programme Aims to Develop

Philosophy

The B.Sc. Agribusiness programme seeks to develop knowledgeable, skilled and entrepreneurial graduates capable of addressing global food-security challenges. It supports the goals of Nigeria’s National Policy on Agriculture by promoting sustainable agricultural practices, increased food production and economic diversification. Through a balance of theory and practical experience, students are prepared to meet evolving sector demands, strengthen supply chains for industrial raw materials, create jobs and improve self-sufficiency and resilience.

Vision

To cultivate visionary agribusiness leaders who advance sustainable agriculture, food security and economic resilience, and position Nigeria more strongly in the global agricultural economy through innovation, entrepreneurship and strategic market solutions.

Objectives

Apply economic principles to address farm-level and national food-production challenges.

Develop knowledge and skills for intellectual growth, research, employment in agribusiness and entrepreneurship.

Contribute to the formulation and improvement of national agricultural policies through research.

Build quantitative and analytical skills, including the use of software to analyse national and global agriculture and food production.

Prepare students for advanced studies in Agricultural Economics and related disciplines.

Produce professionals for Agricultural Officer roles and management and advisory services in government and non-governmental organisations.

Programme Features & Skills
Employability and 21st Century Skills

Employability Skills

Critical thinking and problem-solving in agricultural and business settings.

Independent research, analysis and report writing.

Teamwork, communication and collaboration.

Seminar presentation and professional communication.

Career pathways in research institutes, government, international organisations and agribusiness consulting, as well as opportunities for postgraduate study.

21st Century Skills

Critical thinking and creativity.

Collaboration and communication.

Information, media and technology literacy.

Flexibility, leadership and initiative.

Productivity and social skills.

Unique Features of the Programme

Aligned with Nigeria’s National Policy on Agriculture and wider local, national and global development priorities, extending beyond the minimum BMAS framework.

Uses specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound (SMART) objectives to guide learning outcomes.

Combines economic theory with quantitative and analytical capabilities for careers in academia, research, agricultural services, entrepreneurship and consultancy.

Programme Offered & Duration
B.Sc. Agribusiness

🎓

Bachelor of Science Degree

The programme leads to the Bachelor of Science degree in Agribusiness.

⏱️

Duration

UTME candidates complete a four-year programme (four academic sessions). Direct Entry candidates follow a three-year programme. Candidates with an OND or equivalent qualification and at least Lower Credit may be considered for admission into 200 level.

Programme domicile stated in the supplied curriculum: Department of Agricultural Economics, Faculty of Agriculture. This UniPilot page presents Agribusiness separately in line with the recent Faculty brochure you referenced.

Admission
Admission Requirements

UTME — Four-Year Degree Programme

Candidates must have an acceptable UTME score and five Senior Secondary Certificate (SSCE) credit passes, including English Language, Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, and Biology or Agricultural Science, obtained in not more than two sittings.

UTME subjects:
English, Mathematics or Physics, Chemistry, and Biology or Agricultural Science.

Direct Entry — Three-Year Programme

Candidates must possess five SSCE credit passes, including English Language, and two principal subjects at Advanced GCE level or an NCE/equivalent qualification. Candidates with OND, NCE, JUPEB or IJMB qualifications and relevant credits may be considered for admission into 200 level, subject to the University’s admission requirements.

Graduation
Graduation Requirements & Credit Units

Requirements

Complete and pass all required compulsory and elective courses.

Meet the University, Faculty, Department and Senate requirements for graduation.

Maintain a minimum CGPA of 1.5.

Complete the required research project and other programme requirements.

About the Department
Agricultural Economics

The Department of Agricultural Economics is domiciled in the Faculty of Agriculture at Adekunle Ajasin University. The B.Sc. Agricultural Economics programme combines economic theory with practical agricultural knowledge to prepare graduates to address food security, agricultural productivity, sustainable food systems and economic resilience.

📍 View Department Location

Programme Philosophy, Vision & Objectives
Programme Direction

Philosophy

The B.Sc. Agricultural Economics programme seeks to equip students with analytical skills, an innovative mindset and a global perspective to address food-security challenges. It blends economic theory with practical agricultural insights and prepares graduates for work in academia, research, policy-making and the agricultural industry. Graduates are expected to apply evidence-based approaches to improve productivity, reduce food waste and develop resilient food supply chains in support of food security and sustainable development.

Vision

To develop globally competitive agricultural economists who drive sustainable food systems, enhance productivity and lead innovative solutions for food security and economic resilience worldwide.

Objectives

Develop a skilled workforce with the technology and knowledge needed for productive rural agricultural settings.

Support national self-sufficiency in essential food and agricultural raw materials for industrialisation.

Modernise agricultural production, processing, storage, preservation and distribution.

Expand employment opportunities and improve quality of life in rural communities.

Adapt and apply external technologies to local agricultural management challenges.

Encourage graduates to treat farming as a viable enterprise and exercise sound professional judgement.

Prepare manpower for agricultural production and research across relevant sectors.

Unique Features of the Programme

Aligns with the National Policy on Agriculture and addresses theoretical and practical priorities across local, national and global agricultural value chains.

Uses SMART objectives: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic and Time-bound.

Supports career pathways in agricultural communications, social services, production, finance, sales and marketing.

Prepares graduates for opportunities in agro-processing, agro-allied industries and agri-finance, as well as further study.

Builds specialist knowledge for advanced study and practical problem-solving.

Employability Skills

Self-employment and job creation as agricultural economists or agribusiness enterprise owners.

Professional services in agribusiness, agro-allied industries and agricultural finance.

Manpower for agro-industrial manufacturing.

Roles in agro-allied, marketing and financial sectors.

Collaboration with other specialist sectors to support economic growth and development.

21st-Century Skills

Critical thinking and creativity

Collaboration and communication

Information, media and technology literacy

Flexibility and adaptability

Leadership and initiative

Productivity and social skills

B.Sc. Agricultural Economics

Admission
Admission Requirements

UTME Entry Requirements

In addition to an acceptable UTME score, candidates must have at least five SSCE credit passes, including English Language, Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Biology or Agricultural Science, at not more than two sittings.

Direct Entry Requirements

For the three-year Direct Entry route, candidates must have five SSCE credit passes including English Language, plus two principal passes at Advanced GCE Level or NCE (or equivalent). Holders of OND, NCE, JUPEB or IJMB with credit passes in relevant subjects may be considered for 200 Level entry.

UTME Subject Combination

English Language, Mathematics or Physics, Chemistry, and Biology or Agricultural Science. Candidates should confirm the current approved subject combination with the university and JAMB before applying.

Programme Duration

UTME: four academic sessions (four years). Direct Entry: three academic sessions, with admission normally into 200 Level, subject to applicable requirements.

Graduation
Graduation Requirements

Students must complete and pass the approved compulsory and elective courses and satisfy the university's other graduation conditions.

Introduction & General Background
Department of Agricultural Extension and Rural Development

The Agricultural Extension programme is designed to educate and train undergraduate students seeking a first degree in Agricultural Extension. Its core curriculum provides the academic foundation and practical exposure required to prepare graduates for national and global development, particularly as agriculture and its value chains respond to the opportunities and demands of the Fourth Industrial Revolution.

The programme follows the Core Curriculum and Minimum Academic Standards (CCMAS) for Agricultural Extension while allowing universities to introduce relevant innovations in curriculum content and delivery. At AAUA, the department combines theoretical teaching, practical extension work and rural development activities to improve farmers’ access to useful information and contemporary agricultural practices.

AAUA's Department of Agricultural Extension and Rural Development was established in the 2013/2014 academic session. It works to improve the wellbeing of farmers and rural communities through effective information dissemination, needs-based extension services, research uptake and collaboration with government agencies and non-governmental organisations.

📍 View Faculty Location ↗

Programme Philosophy & Objectives
What the Programme Aims to Develop

Philosophy

The B. Agric. programme is designed to develop globally competitive manpower in agricultural extension and rural development. It equips graduates with comprehensive theoretical knowledge and practical skills to teach farmers and agricultural practitioners contemporary methods, techniques and approaches for productive engagement in agriculture, self-reliance, and national and global development.

Objectives

The programme aims to:

Produce skilled Agricultural Extension Agents who can work effectively in rural settings and address gaps in knowledge of contemporary farming methods.

Support national food self-sufficiency and the production of agricultural raw materials for industry.

Improve rural quality of life through effective agricultural extension education.

Promote the adaptation and adoption of appropriate technologies to solve local agricultural management problems.

Develop graduates with independent thought and sound professional judgement who can provide quality consultancy services to farmers.

Programme Features & Skills
Employability and 21st Century Skills

Employability Skills

Graduates are expected to develop the following workplace and professional capabilities:

Critical thinking and practical problem-solving.

Independent research planning, data gathering and research process management.

Teamwork, collaboration and effective workplace communication.

Entrepreneurship and the ability to provide agricultural consultancy services.

Career opportunities in public and private extension organisations, NGOs, research institutes, government agencies and international organisations.

21st Century Skills

Critical thinking, problem-solving, reasoning, analysis, interpretation and synthesis.

Research practices, inquiry and interrogative questioning.

Leadership, teamwork and collaboration.

Learning and literacy skills.

Oral and written communication and public speaking.

Perseverance, self-direction, planning, self-discipline, adaptability and initiative.

ICT, media and internet literacy, including introductory computer programming.

Unique Features of the Programme

Blended learning that combines face-to-face teaching with virtual learning.

Comprehensive approaches to teaching and learning.

Emphasis on ICT and contemporary global extension platforms for effective agricultural extension service delivery.

Programme Offered & Duration
B. Agric. in Agricultural Extension and Rural Development

🎓

Bachelor of Agriculture Degree

The department awards the B. Agric. degree in Agricultural Extension and Rural Development.

⏱️

Duration

UTME candidates complete a minimum of four academic sessions (four years). Direct Entry candidates admitted into 200 Level complete a minimum of three academic sessions (three years).

Admission
Admission Requirements

UTME — Four-Year Degree Programme

In addition to the required UTME score, candidates must have five credit passes in the Senior Secondary Certificate (SSC) or its equivalent, including English Language, Mathematics, Biology or Agricultural Science, and any two other subjects selected from Chemistry, Physics, Geography and Economics. The credits must be obtained in not more than two sittings.

Direct Entry — Three-Year Programme

Candidates must have at least two Advanced Level credit passes or equivalent in Chemistry and Biology, in addition to the five SSC (or equivalent) credit passes prescribed for UTME entry. Diploma holders with a minimum of Upper Credit and five SSC (or equivalent) credit passes obtained in not more than two sittings are eligible for consideration for admission into 200 Level.

Graduation
Graduation Requirements

To qualify for the award of the B. Agric. degree in Agricultural Extension and Rural Development, a student must complete and pass all registered courses, including all compulsory courses and other requirements prescribed by the University and Faculty.

Students must obtain the minimum CGPA specified by the University, which must not be less than 1.0, and earn at least 120 credit units for the four-year programme or 90 credit units for the three-year Direct Entry programme.

Introduction & General Background
Department of Agronomy

The crop science programme curriculum is designed to impact knowledge in a broad sense in all aspects of crop science, production, produce preservation and utilization. It emphasizes a complete value chain in crop production.

As much as possible, it teaches the deployment of modern technology in meeting the emerging challenges of food insecurity and grooming learners for the development of a sustainable enterprise. An appropriate delivery of the contents of the course modules of this curriculum would produce not just scientists, but equally entrepreneurs in crop production, value addition to crop produce as well as packaging of final crop produce.

📍 View Faculty Location ↗

Programme Philosophy & Objectives
What the Programme Aims to Develop

Philosophy

The principal focus of the national agriculture policy is to strengthen the component parts of the agricultural sector, with particular reference to the crop production sub-sector to meet the demand for food and industrial raw materials. Thus, the philosophy and mission statement underlying the crop science programme of agriculture are aimed at making a positive and significant contribution to the nation's gross domestic product (GDP), and furthering Nigeria's renewed commitment to food sufficiency and general self-reliance through graduates equipped with comprehensive theoretical knowledge and practical skills for meaningful engagement in crop production.

Objectives

The objectives of the programmes in agriculture are in tandem with national needs and priorities. Graduates are expected to be resourceful, creative and knowledgeable in solving relevant societal problems.

Equip graduates with adequate knowledge in the theory and practice of crop production to meet increasing food demand, food security and self-sufficiency.

Enhance national industrialization through increased production of industrial raw materials for a diversified economy.

Advance knowledge in modern production techniques, produce processing and value addition through processing, storage, preservation, transit and distribution.

Improve employability and employment opportunities, reducing social ills resulting from unemployment.

Apply contemporary technology to improve crop production techniques and productivity per land area.

Produce graduates confident in entering practical crop-production enterprises.

Equip graduates with scientific knowledge and background for effective research in crop science.

Programme Features & Skills
Employability and 21st Century Skills

Employability Skills

The curriculum takes due cognizance of employability, developing competence and skills in:

Production enterprise in arable crop farming.

Production enterprise in vegetable crop farming.

Production enterprise in orchard establishment and management.

Enterprise in seed production, processing and packaging.

Consultancy in all aspects of crop production.

Research in crop science and crop improvement.

21st Century Skills

The new CCMAS addresses emerging 21st-century skill gaps in crop science, including:

Critical thinking, problem solving, reasoning, analysis, interpretation and synthesizing information.

Research skills and practices, including interrogative questioning.

Leadership, teamwork and collaboration.

Learning skills and literacy skills.

Oral and written communication and public speaking.

Perseverance, self-direction, planning, self-discipline, adaptability and initiative.

ICT literacy, media and internet literacy, and computer programming.

Unique Features of the Programme

The new crop science programme's philosophy and objectives align with the goals of the national policy on agriculture, making graduates relevant to national and global agricultural development.

The programme provides broad training at lower levels, giving students basic knowledge across agriculture before advanced crop science training in later years.

Practical training is enterprise-based and addresses food and industrial crop supply gaps, contributing to food security.

Programme Offered & Duration
B. Agric. (Honours) in Agronomy

🎓

Bachelor of Agriculture Degree

The programme leads to the B. Agric. (Honours) degree in Agronomy.

⏱️

Duration

UTME candidates spend a minimum of four academic sessions (four years). Direct Entry candidates admitted to 200 level spend a minimum of three academic sessions (three years).

Admission
Admission Requirements

UTME — Four Year Degree Programme

In addition to the UTME score, candidates should possess five credit passes in Senior Secondary Certificate (SSC), including English Language, Mathematics, Biology or Agricultural Science, Chemistry and Physics, in not more than two sittings.

Direct Entry Mode

Candidates must have at least two Advanced Level credit passes or equivalent in Chemistry and Biology, plus the five SSC (or equivalent) credit passes prescribed for UTME entry. Diploma holders with a minimum of Lower Credit, plus the five SSC (or equivalent) credit passes, obtained in not more than two sittings, are eligible for consideration for admission into 200 level.

Graduation
Graduation Requirements

To graduate, a student shall have completed four years of study depending on the entry point, including one practical year or six months of practicals. Activities during the practical period should include periodic seminars on the student's work and the presentation of a written report for grading at the end of the period.

Candidates admitted through UTME must register for at least 120 course units for the four-year track, while Direct Entry candidates must register for at least 84 units for the three-year track, as indicated under course requirements. Candidates must also register and pass all compulsory courses specified for the programme.

Submission of an undergraduate project report based on supervised research is a graduation requirement. It exposes students to problem-solving techniques and develops their ability to organize ideas from literature and research findings, preparing them for post-graduation careers and further postgraduate training.

Introduction & General Background
Animal Science

Welcome to the Department of Animal Science at Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko, Ondo State, Nigeria. The Department provides broad-based, functional and practical training in Animal Science, with emphasis on scientific training, teaching, research, extension and entrepreneurial skills development.

The programme is designed to respond to the needs of the immediate environment and agricultural sustainability by developing appropriate manpower to improve animal production. It prepares students with theoretical knowledge and practical skills to contribute to animal production, research, entrepreneurship, agriculture and national development.

General Overview:
Animal Science is the study of animals that live alongside humans and the science and business of producing domestic livestock species, including beef and dairy cattle, horses, poultry, sheep, goats, swine and rabbits. It also covers companion animals, including their nutrition, care and welfare. The discipline draws on animal behaviour and management, genetics, nutrition, physiology, reproduction and meat science. A broad knowledge base prepares graduates for careers across animal agriculture and related fields.

The programme combines formal scientific training with practical understanding of animal production, care and use. It addresses the biology and management of livestock and companion animals, and the application of scientific knowledge to productive and sustainable animal agriculture.

📍 View Faculty Location ↗

Programme Philosophy & Objectives
What the Programme Aims to Develop

Philosophy

The philosophy that guides the training of students in Animal Science is to adopt practical and realistic approaches to produce skilled manpower furnished with comprehensive knowledge of animal biology and livestock genetic resources, together with the technologies required to improve animal yield and productivity.

The programme seeks to produce graduates with technical, productive and entrepreneurial skills for animal agriculture, livestock farm management and related enterprises, while developing the research inclination needed for careers in academic fields.

Objectives

Produce graduates knowledgeable in animal breeding and genetics, physiology, behaviour and handling, nutrition and biochemistry, husbandry practices, animal health care management, and animal products and by-product technology.

Equip graduates with the skills to establish and profitably operate animal and livestock enterprises.

Contribute to the production of animal-based raw materials for industrial development.

Develop technical and entrepreneurial skills to apply scientific knowledge to practical solutions and advance the animal/livestock subsector.

Develop the capacity to process livestock into useful products and participate across livestock value chains.

Prepare graduates to create demand-driven technologies responsive to local needs and ecological challenges for sustainable animal agriculture and livestock productivity.

Build knowledge of animal-waste management and wealth creation from animal-waste resources.

Unique Features & Employability
Learning, Practical Training & Career Skills

Unique Features of the Programme

Addresses knowledge gaps arising from technological innovations in animal agriculture.

Provides knowledge for the care and management of work and companion animals in line with global trends.

Prepares graduates for present and future animal-production challenges through opportunity identification and innovative solutions.

Encourages entrepreneurship and the development of graduates who can become self-employed or employers.

Includes practical training on animal farms and related enterprises in the fourth year.

Employability Skills

Independent work and research with minimal supervision.

Verbal and written communication, including reports, publications and presentations.

Active listening, interpersonal skills and teamwork.

Time management and meeting deadlines.

Problem-solving and sound decision-making.

Organisation, planning and task coordination.

Ability to learn, adapt and respond to change.

Self-motivation, resilience and pride in achievement.

21st-Century Skills

Curiosity, critical thinking, creativity, collaboration, teamwork, digital literacy, information literacy, communication, media literacy, flexibility, leadership, initiative and social skills.

Programme Offered & Duration
B. Agric. (Animal Science)

🎓

Bachelor of Agriculture in Animal Science

The official programme listed by Adekunle Ajasin University is B. Agric. (Animal Science).

⏱️

Duration

UTME candidates spend a minimum of four academic sessions (four years). Direct Entry candidates admitted into 200 Level spend a minimum of three academic sessions (three years).

Admission
Admission Requirements

UTME Entry Requirements

Obtain the required UTME score and meet the University's admission conditions.

Have five Senior Secondary Certificate (SSC) credit passes, including English Language, Mathematics, Biology or Agricultural Science, Chemistry and Physics.

The five required credits must be obtained in not more than two sittings.

Direct Entry Requirements

At least two A-Level passes or equivalent in Chemistry and Biology, together with the five SSC credit passes prescribed for UTME candidates.

Diploma holders with at least Lower Credit and the required five SSC credits, obtained in not more than two sittings, may be considered for admission into 200 Level.

Graduation
Graduation Requirements

Students must complete the minimum course-unit requirements for their entry route, pass all compulsory and required courses, and fulfil the programme's seminar and research requirements.

Minimum of 125 course units for the four-year UTME programme.

Minimum of 103 course units for the three-year Direct Entry programme.

Attend periodic seminars and submit the required written report for assessment at the end of the year.

Pass all compulsory courses and the required electives.

Complete a supervised undergraduate research project and submit the project report. This develops problem-solving, research, literature-review and report-writing skills.

Registration
Registration for Courses

Course Categories

GST Courses:
General Studies courses required as part of the programme.

ENT Courses:
Entrepreneurship courses included in the programme.

Compulsory Courses:
Courses that students must register for and pass.

Elective Courses:
Approved options from which students select the required number of units.

Course Registration Guidance

Students should register for courses according to their level, semester, entry route and the approved programme structure. The course tables below distinguish compulsory (C) and elective (E) courses and show lecture hours (LH) and practical hours (PH).

WELCOME & BACKGROUND
About the Department

Based on the 2025/2026 Faculty Brochure.

Welcome to Biochemistry at AAUA.
The department's welcome message emphasises academic excellence, innovation and intellectual curiosity. The B.Sc. programme provides broad-based knowledge of chemical processes in living organisms, from single-celled to multicellular plants and animals.

Core areas:
Clinical Biochemistry, Food and Nutritional Biochemistry, Environmental Toxicology, Nutritional Toxicology, Molecular Biology, Bioinformatics and Drug Discovery, and Biotechnology.

Programme philosophy:
Build broad biochemical knowledge, practical laboratory skills, scientific curiosity and an appreciation of biochemistry's contribution to life sciences and wider development.

LEARNING & DEVELOPMENT
Programme Objectives & Skills

Provide broad and balanced biochemical knowledge and practical skills.

Apply knowledge to theoretical and practical problems in biochemistry.

Develop transferable skills for biochemical and non-biochemical employment.

Prepare students for further study in specialised and multidisciplinary areas.

Show the value of interdisciplinary approaches to complex life problems.

Appreciate biochemistry's role in industrial, economic, environmental, technological and social development.

Unique programme features
Develops cognitive abilities in biochemistry and related sciences.

Introduces tropical flora and fauna and potential uses in drug development.

Builds laboratory and instrumentation skills.

Develops scientific information literacy and independent learning.

Strengthens critical thinking for industrial, environmental and life-science problems.

Employability skills
Critical thinking, problem-solving, analysis and interpretation.

Creativity, innovation and personal expression.

Research, scientific questioning and inquiry.

Oral and written communication.

ICT literacy and data analysis.

Understanding of industrial biochemical processes.

Entrepreneurship and small/medium enterprise development.

Programme Offered & Duration
Degree Programme

Programme details based on the supplied 2025/2026 Faculty Brochure.

🧬

B.Sc. Biochemistry

Study the chemical processes and molecular mechanisms that sustain living organisms, with practical training across biological and chemical sciences.

⏳

Normal Duration

4 years for UTME candidates and 3 years for Direct Entry candidates, subject to current university regulations.

ENTRY REQUIREMENTS
Admission Requirements

Confirm current requirements with AAUA before applying.

UTME · 100 Level

Five SSCE/SSC or equivalent credit passes at not more than two sittings, including English Language, Mathematics, Biology, Chemistry and Physics, plus an acceptable UTME result.

Direct Entry · 200 Level

The brochure says candidates with five SSCE (or equivalent) credit passes and at least two relevant advanced-level passes in Biology and Chemistry through GCE Advanced Level, IJMB or JUPEB may be considered. Confirm current rules with AAUA Admissions.

Academic Regulations
Examination, Grading & Degree Classification

The grading scale and degree-classification ranges below are the same as those used on the Geology and Applied Geophysics pages. Confirm current regulations with AAUA.

Assessment

Continuous assessment contributes 30% and the final semester examination contributes 70%. Final-year project scripts and oral examinations are moderated or conducted by external examiners.

Welcome & Background
About the Department

Welcome to Chemistry at AAUA.

Chemistry explores the composition, structure and properties of matter, the changes matter undergoes, and the energy involved in those changes. This page focuses on the B.Sc. Chemistry programme and presents the course structure supplied in the 2025/2026 Faculty Brochure.

Department background:
The Department of Chemical Sciences, formerly known as the Department of Chemistry and Industrial Chemistry, was among the pioneer departments in the Faculty of Science when the university relocated from Ado-Ekiti to its present site at Akungba-Akoko. The department offers B.Sc. Chemistry and B.Sc. Industrial Chemistry. Uni Pilot presents these as separate guides to make each programme easier to find.

Study areas:
Organic, inorganic, analytical and physical chemistry, spectroscopy, environmental and green chemistry, natural products, polymers, materials, and applied chemical research.

📍 View Department Location · Coming soon
Official department page:
AAUA Department of Chemical Sciences
. Exact map pin will be added after it is confirmed by the Uni Pilot team.

Programme Philosophy & Objectives
What the Programme Aims to Develop

This is a student-friendly summary of the Chemistry programme's study areas, not a quotation of an official philosophy statement.

Programme Philosophy

To build a sound foundation in chemical principles and scientific reasoning, supported by practical laboratory skills, analysis, research and an understanding of how chemistry applies to materials, the environment and everyday life.

Learning Objectives

Develop a sound understanding of fundamental chemical principles.

Build competence in laboratory practice, observation, measurement and chemical analysis.

Understand chemical structures, reactions, kinetics and mechanisms.

Apply chemistry to environmental, material, industrial and other practical problems.

Develop research, data interpretation, communication and problem-solving skills.

Prepare students for further study and relevant scientific careers.

Programme Offered & Duration
Degree Programme

Industrial Chemistry has its own separate Uni Pilot page.

🎓

B.Sc. Chemistry

Undergraduate programme in fundamental and applied chemistry, including theory, practical laboratory work and a final-year research project.

⏱️

Normal Duration

UTME entry: 4 years (8 semesters). Direct Entry: 3 years (6 semesters), subject to the applicable university regulations.

🔬

Core Study Areas

Organic, inorganic, physical and analytical chemistry, spectroscopy, environmental chemistry, green chemistry and chemical research.

🧪

Practical Learning

Laboratory practicals, industrial attachment listed in the course structure, seminar and research project work.

Admission
Admission Requirements

Requirements transcribed from the supplied 2025/2026 Faculty Brochure. Applicants should confirm the current requirements with AAUA and JAMB.

UTME Entry Requirements

Five O’Level credit passes in not more than two sittings.

Required subjects: English Language, Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics, and Biology or Agricultural Science.

Normal programme duration: four years.

Direct Entry Requirements

A’Level passes in Chemistry and Physics or Mathematics; or

OND/HND Upper Credit in a relevant field, as stated in the supplied brochure.

Normal programme duration: three years.

Maximum Duration

The supplied brochure states a maximum of two additional sessions beyond the normal duration: up to 10 semesters for UTME entry and up to 8 semesters for Direct Entry.

Introduction & General Background
Computer Science

Welcome to the Department of Computer Science at Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko, Ondo State, Nigeria.

The supplied department handbook describes the Department of Computer Science as an academic unit established to produce highly trained graduates in Computer Science and Information Technology. It notes the department's commitment to teaching, mentoring, research and technological development.

The B.Sc. Computer Science programme covers basic and applied computing and information technology, including the algorithmic process and computational machines, hardware and software systems, computer programming, systems analysis and software development.

The programme aims to prepare graduates who can understand the impact and applications of computing and contribute to public and industrial sectors.

Dr. Mrs E. O. Aliyu
Head of Department

📍 View Department Location ↗

Programme Philosophy & Objectives
What the Programme Aims to Develop

Philosophy

The philosophy of the Computer Science programme is to provide broad, high-quality education that emphasises the theoretical and algorithmic foundations of computing, guiding the design, implementation and application of computational systems.

The programme is designed to give students broad Computer Science knowledge and the opportunity to tailor their studies to their interests and needs across academic and industrial fields.

Objectives

Build students' awareness of and enthusiasm for Computer Science and its capabilities.

Provide a broad and balanced foundation of Computer Science knowledge and practical skills.

Develop the ability to formulate real-world computing problems and use appropriate tools and technologies to find valid solutions.

Develop students' ability to analyse, evaluate and propose alternative software or algorithm designs.

Encourage self-management, teamwork, professional and ethical practice, effective communication and lifelong learning.

Programme Offered & Duration
B.Sc. Computer Science

🎓

Bachelor of Science Degree in Computer Science

The programme offered is the Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Science.

⏱️

Duration

Candidates admitted through UTME normally spend a minimum of 4 years, while Direct Entry candidates normally spend a minimum of 3 years.

Admission
Admission Requirements

UTME Entry Requirements

Five O'Level credit passes at SSCE (WAEC, GCE, NECO or NABTEB), in not more than two sittings, including English Language, Mathematics and Physics, plus two from Chemistry, Biology/Agricultural Science, Statistics, Additional Mathematics, Computer Studies, ICT or Basic Electronics.

UTME subjects must include Mathematics, Physics and one of Biology, Chemistry, Agricultural Science, Economics, Geography or Computer Studies.

Candidates successful in the Science pre-degree programme of Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko may also be considered.

Direct Entry Requirements

Applicants seeking admission into 200 level must satisfy the O'Level requirements and one of the following:

Passes in two A'Level subjects, including Mathematics.

At least an Upper Credit in ND Computer Science, Statistics or Electronics/Electrical Engineering.

NCE with at least a Merit in Computer Science, Mathematics or Statistics.

Graduation
Graduation Requirements

Pass all core courses and required university and faculty/school courses.

Accumulate at least 140 course units for UTME entry or 108 course units for Direct Entry students admitted at 200 level, as stated in the supplied handbook.

Attain a minimum CGPA of 1.00.

Be found worthy in character and complete the prescribed Core, Faculty, General Studies, SIWES, Seminar and Final Year Project requirements.

Registration
Registration for Courses

Course Categories

Compulsory Courses:
Courses which students must offer and pass before graduation.

Elective Courses:
Departmental-prescribed courses required to be registered and passed to meet the minimum requirements of the University before graduation.

Registration Rules

The minimum work load is 15 units and the maximum is 28 units per semester.

A student can withdraw from a course within the time stipulated by Senate without penalty only with the approval of the HOD on completion of Add and Delete form.

Any student who withdraws without due permission will be deemed to have failed the course.

Any course examination sat for without registration will be cancelled.

About the Faculty

Welcome to the Faculty of Computing at Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko, a community of innovators, thinkers, and problem-solvers preparing students for the opportunities and challenges of the digital age.

The Faculty is committed to providing a strong learning environment in computing and related digital disciplines. Its academic areas include software development, artificial intelligence, data science, information and communication technology, information systems, and cybersecurity.

Students are encouraged to develop practical skills, critical thinking, creativity, collaboration, and problem-solving abilities while learning from academic staff and researchers.

Explore the departments below to discover the programmes and academic information available within the Faculty of Computing.

Programmes

B.Sc. Computer Science
Study computing principles, programming, algorithms, software, systems, and related areas of computer science.

B.Sc. Cyber Security
Focus on protecting computer systems, networks, applications, data, and digital environments.

B.Sc. Data Science
Explore data analysis, computational methods, statistics, and techniques for extracting useful insights from data.

B.Sc. Information and Communication Technology
Study digital technologies, communication systems, information processing, and ICT applications.

B.Sc. Information Systems
Explore the design and use of information systems that support organisations, people, and business processes.

B.Sc. Software Engineering
Focus on software development, software design, testing, maintenance, and engineering practices.

Introduction & General Background
Department of Cyber Security

It is with great pleasure and a deep sense of responsibility that I welcome you all to the Department of Cyber Security. In an era where technology continues to evolve at an unprecedented pace, the importance of cybersecurity cannot be overstated. Cyber threats, data breaches, and digital vulnerabilities pose substantial risks to individuals, organisations, and nations. It is our collective duty to stay ahead of these threats through continuous learning, research, and innovation.

The supplied prospectus states that the Department of Cyber Security emerged with the Faculty of Computing in July 2024. The department aims to foster excellence, collaboration, and technological advancement through a blend of theoretical foundations and practical applications.

Students are encouraged to engage in research, participate in cybersecurity competitions, collaborate on innovative projects, and develop the skills needed to contribute to this evolving field.

Dr. D. A. Akinwumi
Ag. HOD, Cyber Security

General Overview

Recent developments in computing, network technologies, the internet and cloud technologies have increased the need for reliable and secure exchange of digital information. As the use of information technology expands, so do the potential consequences of cyber-attacks and the need for skilled professionals who can prevent and respond to them. Government agencies, businesses, industries and the military need qualified professionals to safeguard their systems, businesses and infrastructure.

Programme Philosophy & Objectives
What the Programme Aims to Develop

Programme focus

The programme aims to equip students with sufficient knowledge and skills to minimise and prevent cybersecurity threats and incidents. Students are also equipped to gather, analyse and present evidence of cybersecurity breaches professionally, and to identify and implement security practices that enhance the security of computers, computer-based systems and cyberspace.

Philosophy

The philosophy of the programme is to build capacity and develop human capital in cybersecurity to safeguard business transactions, corporate assets, critical infrastructure and cyber operations nationally and globally.

Objectives

Produce graduates with foundational cybersecurity knowledge, skills and strategies to detect and prevent cyber-fraud.

Enable graduates to analyse cybersecurity threats, attacks and risks and develop detection code and supportive software agents.

Develop knowledge of cryptography, steganography and digital forensic science techniques for detecting cybercrimes.

Develop critical thinking about cyber-intelligence security issues and cybersecurity strategies, drawing on case studies.

Prepare graduates for self-employment, cybersecurity jobs and professional practice in government and industry.

Programme and duration

The programme offered is the Bachelor of Science Degree in Cyber Security.

UTME entry:
minimum 4 years.

Direct Entry:
minimum 3 years.

Admission
Admission Requirements

These requirements follow the supplied transcription. Confirm them with the current university admission notice before applying.

UTME Entry Requirements

Five O'Level credit passes at SSCE (WAEC, GCE, NECO or NABTEB) in no more than two sittings, including English Language, Mathematics and Physics, plus two from Chemistry, Biology/Agricultural Science, Additional Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Studies, ICT or Basic Electronics.

The transcript states that UTME subjects must include Mathematics, Physics and one of Biology, Chemistry, Agricultural Science, Economics or Geography, and also says “AND Computer Studies”. This wording is ambiguous in the source and should be checked against the official current requirements.

Candidates successful in the science pre-degree programme of Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko may also be considered.

Source wording note:
The prospectus heading for the minimum entry requirements refers to “B.Sc Degree in Computer Science” even though this is the Cyber Security section.

Direct Entry Requirements

The transcript describes students entering 200 level and lists these options, provided the stated O'Level requirements are met:

Passes in two A-Level subjects, including Mathematics.

At least Upper Credit in an ND in Computer Science, Statistics or Electronics/Electrical Engineering.

NCE with at least Merit in Computer Science, Mathematics or Statistics may also be considered.

The source refers to the “Computer Science degree programme” in this section. Confirm the wording with the department.

Graduation
Graduation Requirements

Pass all core courses, University and Faculty/School required courses, and electives.

Accumulate at least
149 course units
for students admitted through UTME or
117 course units
for students admitted to 200 level through Direct Entry.

Attain a minimum CGPA of
1.00
.

Be found worthy in character throughout studentship and complete the prescribed units from Core, Faculty and General Studies courses, as well as SIWES, Seminar and Final Year Project.

Registration for Courses
Course Categories & Registration Rules

Course categories

Compulsory courses:
courses students must offer and pass before graduation.

Elective courses:
departmental-prescribed courses that students register for and pass to meet University requirements before graduation.

Registration rules

Minimum workload: 15 units per semester.

Maximum workload: 28 units per semester.

A student may withdraw from a course within the Senate-stipulated period without penalty only with HOD approval and completion of an Add and Delete form.

Withdrawal without permission is treated as failure.

An examination taken for a course that was not registered will be cancelled.

Introduction & General Background
Data Science & Artificial Intelligence

I am delighted to welcome you to the Department of Data Science & Artificial Intelligence, Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko, Ondo State, Nigeria.

The Department of Data Science evolved to become a unique academic unit in the University. It is supported by dedicated academic and non-academic staff committed to high standards of teaching, mentoring and research.

Our programmes expose students to basic and applied courses in Computing and Data Science, as well as Industrial Training, to prepare graduates for manpower needs in the public and industrial sectors.

The department trains competent Artificial Intelligence and Data Science experts and related professionals for national manpower needs and technological development.

Dr. Oluwafemi Oriola
HOD – Data Science & Artificial Intelligence

General Overview

Organisations accumulate large quantities of data for market research, disaster prediction, investment analysis, manufacturing, sales, customer behaviour, security intelligence, policy development, artificial intelligence and healthcare. Data scientists use analytical and technical skills to harvest intelligence from data and support decision-making.

Programme competencies include computational and statistical thinking, mathematical foundations, model building and assessment, data curation, knowledge transference, analytics and information management.

Programme Philosophy & Objectives
What the Programme Aims to Develop

Philosophy

To equip Data Science students with the foundations, methods and implications of data science, extracting knowledge from data using techniques and theories from Mathematics, Statistics, Computing and Information Technology. The programme provides broad knowledge of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence for academic and industry pathways.

Objectives

Develop skills to analyse computationally intensive real-life problems and independently build data-driven solutions.

Build competence in the four A's of data: architecture, acquisition, analysis and archiving.

Train students to discover information in data across business, government, healthcare, education, data engineering, big data and analytics.

Prepare students to integrate data-driven IT solutions and business processes to meet organisational information needs effectively.

Programme Offered & Duration
B.Sc. Data Science

🎓

Bachelor of Science Degree in Data Science

The programme offered is Bachelor of Science Degree in Data Science.

⏱️

Duration

UTME: 4 years minimum. Direct Entry: 3 years minimum.

Admission
Admission Requirements

UTME Entry Requirements

Five O'Level credits at SSCE (WAEC, GCE, NECO or NABTEB), in no more than two sittings, including English Language, Mathematics, Physics and at least one of Chemistry, Biology/Agricultural Science, Statistics, Additional Mathematics, Economics, Geography, Computer Studies, ICT or Basic Electronics.

UTME subjects: Use of English, Mathematics, Physics and one of Biology, Chemistry, Agricultural Science, Economics, Geography or Computer Studies.

Successful candidates from the AAUA pre-degree programme (Science) may also be considered.

Direct Entry Requirements

Applicants entering 200 Level must satisfy one of the following, subject to the O'Level requirement:

Passes in two A'Level subjects, including Mathematics.

At least Upper Credit in ND Computer Science, Statistics or Electronics/Electrical Engineering.

NCE with at least Merit in Computer Science, Mathematics or Statistics.

The prospectus admission subsection is headed “B.Sc Degree in Computer Science”; the programme title, surrounding text and stated award identify this as the B.Sc. Data Science programme. The page therefore uses the consistent programme title.

Graduation
Graduation Requirements

Pass all core courses, University and Faculty/School required courses, and electives.

Accumulate at least 145 course units for UTME admission or 115 course units for Direct Entry admission, as stated in this section of the prospectus.

Attain a minimum CGPA of 1.00.

Be found worthy in character and complete prescribed Core, Faculty, General Studies, SIWES, Seminar and Final Year Project requirements.

The programme summary elsewhere states 147 units for the four-year programme. This conflicts with the 145-unit graduation requirement.

Registration
Registration for Courses

Course Categories

Compulsory:
Courses students must offer and pass before graduation.

Elective:
Department-prescribed courses required to meet University graduation requirements.

Registration Rules

Minimum workload: 15 units per semester.

Maximum workload: 28 units per semester.

Withdrawal within the Senate-approved period requires HOD approval and completion of an Add and Delete form.

Withdrawal without due permission is treated as failure.

An examination taken for an unregistered course will be cancelled.

About the Department
Fisheries and Aquaculture

The Department of Fisheries and Aquaculture is part of the Faculty of Agriculture at Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko, Ondo State, Nigeria. The programme prepares students with the scientific knowledge, technical competence and practical skills required across capture fisheries and aquaculture.

Fisheries and aquaculture contribute to food and nutritional security, employment, livelihoods and foreign-exchange earnings. The programme also considers the role of aquatic resources in sustainable development and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.

Its training is designed to prepare graduates for entrepreneurship, employment, research and further studies, while responding to national needs and the changing global fisheries and aquaculture industry.

📍 View Department Location

Programme Philosophy, Objectives & Skills
Programme Direction

Philosophy

The programme provides general and in-depth knowledge in different areas of Fisheries and Aquaculture, with emphasis on applying the discipline to food and nutrition security, employment and livelihoods, and sustainable ecological and socio-economic development. Students are trained in qualitative and quantitative approaches through a multidisciplinary perspective.

Objectives

Produce proficient graduates with broad fisheries knowledge to meet national high-level manpower needs, with an orientation towards entrepreneurship and self-employment.

Provide theoretical and technical knowledge across fisheries and aquaculture, and the ability to apply analytical tools to societal and economic problems.

Equip graduates with current techniques for sustainable fish production and careers in River Basin Authorities, government ministries, industrial fish firms, fish farms and development agencies.

Prepare graduates for postgraduate studies in specialist areas of Fisheries and Aquaculture.

Unique Features

Training in both capture fisheries and fish culture (aquaculture).

Coverage of the environmental, economic and social pillars of sustainability.

Courses spanning upstream and downstream activities across the fisheries and aquaculture value chain.

Newer subject areas include the Blue Economy and Entrepreneurship in Fisheries and Aquaculture.

Employability Skills

Critical thinking and problem-solving.

Communication and presentation.

Creativity, innovation and entrepreneurship.

Teamwork, collaboration and interpersonal communication.

Self-management, planning, organisation and task management.

Leadership, accountability and social responsibility.

21st-Century Skills

Communication

Critical thinking

Problem-solving

Collaboration

Programme Offered & Duration
B. Fisheries and Aquaculture

🎓

UTME Programme

A four-year degree programme leading to the award of B. Fisheries and Aquaculture.

🐟

Direct Entry

Eligible diploma holders may be considered for admission into 200 Level, subject to the stated entry requirements.

Admission
Admission Requirements

UTME Entry Requirements

In addition to an acceptable UTME score, candidates must possess five SSCE credit passes, including English Language, Mathematics, Biology or Agricultural Science, Chemistry and Physics, in not more than two sittings.

Direct Entry Requirements

Candidates must have at least two credit passes at Advanced Level or equivalent in Chemistry and Biology, in addition to five prescribed SSCE credit passes. Diploma holders in Fisheries and Aquaculture or a related field with at least Lower Credit, plus the required SSCE credits, may be considered for 200 Level.

Programme Duration

UTME: four years. Direct Entry: admission may be into 200 Level, subject to the university's applicable requirements.

Degree Award

B. Fisheries and Aquaculture.

Graduation
Graduation Requirements

Students must complete and pass the required courses and satisfy the university's other graduation conditions.

UTME:
128 credit units, comprising 8 GST units, 4 ENT units and 116 compulsory units.

Direct Entry:
a minimum of 102 credit units, comprising 8 GST units, 4 ENT units, 4 AGR units and 90 compulsory units.

Introduction & General Background
Food Science and Technology

Welcome to the Department of Food Science and Technology, Faculty of Agriculture, Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko. The Department is committed to developing knowledgeable, skilled and innovative graduates who can contribute to food production, processing, preservation, quality assurance and the advancement of the food industry.

Food Science and Technology is an interdisciplinary field applying scientific and engineering principles to food processing, preservation, packaging, storage, distribution, analysis and evaluation. It examines the physical, chemical, biological and nutritional properties of food and develops ways to improve food quality, safety, availability and consumer acceptability.

The programme addresses food security and post-harvest challenges by preparing graduates to transform agricultural raw materials into safe, nutritious and marketable food products. It combines theoretical instruction with practical learning, laboratory experiments, food analysis, processing activities and product development.

📍 View Department Location ↗

Programme Philosophy, Aim & Objectives
What the Programme Aims to Develop

Philosophy

The programme responds to the need for skilled manpower in preserving agricultural crops and developing food products and processes that provide nutritious and balanced diets. It applies science and engineering to food processing, preservation, packaging, storage, distribution, analysis and the design and evaluation of food systems and machinery.

Its philosophy is to produce graduates with strong academic standards and practical competence in food science and post-harvest management, prepared for self-employment and valuable service to industry, academia and the wider community in support of global food security.

Aim

The programme aims to support the National Policy on Agriculture and Nigeria's commitment to food sufficiency and self-reliance. It prepares graduates with theoretical knowledge and practical skills for meaningful work in food management, processing and technology, enabling them to become self-reliant and valuable contributors to industry and society.

Programme Objectives

Train skilled technical and managerial manpower for agro-allied industries.

Prepare graduates to establish, manage and direct small-scale food-processing and related industries using locally available raw materials.

Develop personnel for consultancy, product development, research, processing and preservation to reduce post-harvest losses.

Equip graduates with knowledge of food-processing equipment design and fabrication and the development of traditional technology.

Prepare graduates for postgraduate study and teaching in Food Science and Technology and related disciplines.

Contribute to national self-sufficiency in basic food and agricultural raw materials needed for industrialisation.

Support modernisation of agricultural production, processing, storage, preservation and distribution.

Improve employment opportunities and contribute to rural development and quality of life.

Develop professional judgement and entrepreneurial ability to establish small- and medium-scale enterprises.

Produce manpower for research and for production, quality assurance and quality-control management in food-processing industries.

Training & Career Development
Learning, Practical Training & Employability

Food Sector Skills

Food quality management, quality assurance and quality control.

Food safety management, hygiene, legislation and control.

Research and development, product development, consumer and nutritional science.

Food production operations, manufacturing management, engineering maintenance, health, safety and environmental practices.

Food retail, supply-chain logistics, transportation and food-service support.

Food processing and manufacturing, including meat and poultry processing.

Employability & Career Opportunities

Research and development officer in food industries.

Food production, processing and quality assurance/control manager.

Consultant assessing food-processing plants and recommending good manufacturing practices.

Entrepreneur establishing cottage or small-scale food-processing businesses.

Food inspection and regulatory roles with agencies such as NAFDAC and the Standards Organisation of Nigeria.

Food-processing equipment design and construction.

Teaching and research in appropriate institutions.

Opportunities with food and agriculture organisations, including FAO, subject to recruitment requirements.

Five 21st-Century Priority Skills

Product development.

Food legislation and control, and food safety management.

Food hygiene and food safety control.

Quality management, quality assurance and quality control.

Research.

Programme Offered & Duration
B.Sc. Food Science and Technology

🎓

Bachelor of Science

The degree awarded is Bachelor of Science in Food Science and Technology (B.Sc. Food Science and Technology).

⏱️

Programme Duration

UTME candidates: five academic sessions (five years). Direct Entry candidates: four academic sessions (four years), subject to approved entry level and admission conditions.

Admission
Admission Requirements

UTME Entry Requirements

Meet the University's UTME admission conditions.

Obtain at least five SSCE credit passes, including English Language, Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, and Biology or Agricultural Science.

The five required credits must be obtained in not more than two sittings.

UTME subject combination:
English Language, Mathematics or Physics, Chemistry, and Biology or Agricultural Science.

Direct Entry Requirements

Five SSCE credit passes, including English Language, plus two principal passes in relevant subjects at Advanced GCE, NCE or equivalent level.

OND, NCE, JUPEB or IJMB holders with credit passes in relevant subjects may be considered for admission into 200 Level.

HND holders with Upper Credit may be considered for admission into 300 Level.

Note:
The supplied text also mentions OND/HND or equivalent with at least Lower Credit for advanced placement. Confirm the exact entry level and minimum qualification with AAUA Admissions.

Graduation
Graduation Requirements

Students must complete and pass the approved compulsory and elective courses, meet the minimum credit-unit requirements for their entry route, and satisfy departmental and University regulations.

UTME students: minimum of 182 credit units.

Direct Entry students: minimum of 156 credit units.

Complete all compulsory courses and required elective units.

Obtain a minimum CGPA of 1.50.

Meet any additional requirements prescribed by the Department and Senate.

The supplied Direct Entry level table has incomplete or misaligned entries at 100 Level. The stated overall minimum of 156 units is retained pending confirmation.

Registration
Course Status & Registration Guidance

Course Categories

Compulsory (C):
Core courses that must be taken and passed.

Required (R):
Courses that must be taken and passed.

Elective (E):
Approved options students may select to meet the minimum credit-unit requirement.

University Courses:
University courses are treated as required courses.

Course Registration

Register for courses according to the approved level and semester structure, entry route and departmental guidance. The tables preserve the First Semester and Second Semester arrangement printed in the programme document.

Confirm elective choices and course-code or title discrepancies with the Department before registration.

Assessment
Evaluation of Students' Performance

Course Assessment

Each course is graded out of 100 marks.

Continuous assessment accounts for 30%.

The end-of-course examination accounts for 70%.

The minimum pass mark is 40%.

Introduction & General Background
Department of Forestry and Wildlife Management

Welcome to the Department of Forestry and Wildlife Management, Faculty of Agriculture, Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko, Ondo State, Nigeria. The Department prepares students for the sustainable management and conservation of forest and wildlife resources.

The programme provides training in the scientific use, conservation and productivity of renewable natural resources. It addresses major environmental challenges such as deforestation, desertification, biodiversity loss and climate change, while developing graduates who can contribute to sustainable development and establish forestry and wildlife-related enterprises.

The curriculum covers the management of natural and man-made forests, wildlife resources, forest products and conservation practices. It also exposes students to practical and entrepreneurial opportunities in urban forestry, ecotourism, timber harvesting, wood-products processing and Geographic Information Systems (GIS).

📍 View Faculty Location ↗

Programme Philosophy & Objectives
What the Programme Aims to Develop

Philosophy

The programme is designed to produce graduates with comprehensive theoretical knowledge and practical skills for the sustainable management, conservation and productive use of forest and wildlife resources. It promotes scientific resource management, environmental protection, self-employment and the development of technical, research and entrepreneurial skills in forestry and wildlife management.

Objectives

The programme aims to:

Equip graduates with skills for sustainable management of forest and wildlife resources and the establishment of independent enterprises.

Support local and global initiatives for sustainable development of renewable natural resources.

Contribute to diversification and transformation of the national economy through forestry and wildlife-related activities.

Promote climate-change mitigation, biodiversity conservation and ecological stability.

Develop technical, productive, research and entrepreneurial skills relevant to the discipline.

Prepare graduates to contribute to industry, communities and national development through responsible resource use.

Programme Features & Skills
Employability and 21st Century Skills

Employability Skills

Forest establishment, management and regeneration.

Plant propagation, seedling production and nursery management.

Wildlife conservation, habitat management and game management.

Forest products processing, timber harvesting and utilization.

Ecotourism, urban forestry and natural-resource consultancy.

GIS, remote sensing, field research and environmental assessment.

Entrepreneurship and management of forestry and wildlife enterprises.

21st Century Skills

Critical thinking, problem-solving and research skills.

Communication, report writing and presentation.

Teamwork, collaboration and leadership.

Digital literacy, information literacy and use of GIS technologies.

Adaptability, initiative, time management and self-direction.

Environmental awareness, innovation and responsible decision-making.

Unique Features of the Programme

Training in the conservation and sustainable use of renewable natural resources.

Exposure to specialist areas such as urban forestry, wood-products processing, ecological conservation, ecotourism, timber harvesting and GIS.

Practical and field-based learning that connects classroom knowledge with forestry and wildlife management activities.

Preparation for self-employment, enterprise development and professional careers in natural-resource management.

Programme Offered & Duration
Bachelor of Forestry

🎓

Bachelor of Forestry

The Faculty of Agriculture lists Forestry and Wildlife Management under its Bachelor of Forestry programme.

⏱️

Duration

UTME candidates spend a minimum of four academic sessions (four years). Direct Entry candidates admitted to 200 level spend a minimum of three academic sessions (three years).

Admission
Admission Requirements

UTME — Four-Year Degree Programme

Candidates should possess five Senior Secondary Certificate credit passes in English Language, Mathematics, Chemistry, Biology and Agricultural Science, in not more than two sittings, alongside a pass in Physics, and must meet the current UTME requirements.

Duration:
Minimum of four academic sessions.

Direct Entry Mode

The programme summary supplied for this department describes eligibility through relevant Advanced Level passes in Chemistry and Biology together with the required O’Level credits, or relevant National Diploma, NCE or HND qualifications with at least Lower Credit for consideration for admission into 200 level.

Duration:
Minimum of three academic sessions.

Applicants should confirm current subject combinations and accepted qualifications against the latest JAMB brochure and AAUA admission notice.

Graduation
Graduation Requirements

Students are expected to complete the approved course requirements for their entry route and pass all compulsory courses specified for the programme.

The programme summary used for this department page specifies a minimum of
120 credit units
for UTME candidates and
90 credit units
for Direct Entry candidates. Students should confirm the applicable total and current regulations with the Department before final course registration.

Students must also complete the approved practical and research requirements, including the supervised undergraduate project report where specified by the department. The project develops problem-solving, literature review, research and report-writing skills.

Compulsory Courses:
Courses marked C are compulsory and must be completed as specified for the programme.

Elective Courses:
Courses marked E are electives. Students should select electives according to the department's approved course-registration guidance.

Welcome & Background
About the Department

Welcome to Geology at AAUA.
This page focuses on the B.Sc. (Hons.) Geology programme and presents the course structure supplied in the 2025/2026 Faculty Brochure.

Department background:
The Department of Earth Sciences was formerly the Department of Geology. It was established in 1982 at Ondo State University, Ado-Ekiti, and relocated to Akungba-Akoko in December 1999. Applied Geophysics was introduced as a separate degree programme. Senate approved the name Department of Earth Sciences on 27 November 2013.

Both Geology and Applied Geophysics are reported in the supplied brochure as NUC-accredited/verified and COMEG-certified programmes.

📍 Department Location · Details to confirm
Official department page and direct links will be added after verification.

Programme Philosophy & Objectives
What the Programme Aims to Develop

Programme Philosophy

To develop enthusiasm and practical skills in geological studies, problem-solving in theoretical and field geology, and preparation for work in petroleum, groundwater, mineral prospecting, civil engineering and environmental sectors.

Programme Objectives

Build strong scientific and practical skills.

Develop field, laboratory, analytical and problem-solving abilities.

Prepare students for research, further study and relevant geoscience careers.

Develop competence in interpreting Earth materials and processes or geophysical data, according to the programme.

Admission
Admission Requirements

Transcribed from the supplied 2025/2026 Faculty Brochure. Confirm current requirements with AAUA and JAMB before applying.

UTME Entry

Five O’Level credit passes at not more than two sittings: English Language, Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Biology.

UTME subjects: English, Chemistry and Physics, plus Biology or Mathematics.

Direct Entry

Advanced-level passes in at least two of Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology and Physics; or

ND in relevant Geosciences with Upper Credit.

Programme Duration & Credit Requirements

UTME/Pre-Degree: 4 years (8 semesters), minimum 120 credit units. Direct Entry: 3 years (6 semesters), minimum 90 credit units. The brochure states 15–28 credit units per semester and at least 30 credit units per session.

Academic Regulations
Examination, Grading & Degree Classification

Assessment

Continuous assessment contributes 30% and the final semester examination contributes 70%. Final-year project scripts and oral examinations are moderated or conducted by external examiners.

Welcome & Background
About the Department

Welcome to Applied Geophysics at AAUA.
This page focuses on the B.Sc. (Hons.) Applied Geophysics programme and presents the course structure supplied in the 2025/2026 Faculty Brochure.

Department background:
The Department of Earth Sciences was formerly the Department of Geology. It was established in 1982 at Ondo State University, Ado-Ekiti, and relocated to Akungba-Akoko in December 1999. Applied Geophysics was introduced as a separate degree programme. Senate approved the name Department of Earth Sciences on 27 November 2013.

Both Geology and Applied Geophysics are reported in the supplied brochure as NUC-accredited/verified and COMEG-certified programmes.

📍 Department Location · Details to confirm
Official department page and direct links will be added after verification.

Programme Philosophy & Objectives
What the Programme Aims to Develop

Programme Philosophy

To provide a robust foundation in exploration geophysics, hydrocarbon and groundwater exploration, environmental pollution and site investigation, dam and road construction studies, and clean-energy technologies.

Programme Objectives

Build strong scientific and practical skills.

Develop field, laboratory, analytical and problem-solving abilities.

Prepare students for research, further study and relevant geoscience careers.

Develop competence in interpreting Earth materials and processes or geophysical data, according to the programme.

Admission
Admission Requirements

Transcribed from the supplied 2025/2026 Faculty Brochure. Confirm current requirements with AAUA and JAMB before applying.

UTME Entry

Five O’Level credit passes at not more than two sittings: English Language, Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Biology.

UTME subjects: English, Chemistry and Physics, plus Biology or Mathematics.

Direct Entry

Advanced-level passes in Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry; or

ND/HND Upper Credit in Civil, Geological, Electrical/Electronic Engineering or another relevant physical science/engineering course.

Programme Duration & Credit Requirements

UTME/Pre-Degree: 4 years (8 semesters), minimum 120 credit units. Direct Entry: 3 years (6 semesters), minimum 90 credit units. The brochure states 15–28 credit units per semester and at least 30 credit units per session.

Academic Regulations
Examination, Grading & Degree Classification

Assessment

Continuous assessment contributes 30% and the final semester examination contributes 70%. Final-year project scripts and oral examinations are moderated or conducted by external examiners.
