About the Department

Welcome to Industrial Chemistry at AAUA.

Chemistry explores the composition, structure and properties of matter, the changes matter undergoes, and the energy involved in those changes. This page focuses on the B.Sc. Industrial Chemistry programme and presents the course structure supplied in the 2025/2026 Faculty Brochure.

Department background:
The Department of Chemical Sciences, formerly known as the Department of Chemistry and Industrial Chemistry, was among the pioneer departments in the Faculty of Science when the university relocated from Ado-Ekiti to its present site at Akungba-Akoko. The department offers B.Sc. Chemistry and B.Sc. Industrial Chemistry. Uni Pilot presents these as separate guides to make each programme easier to find.

Study areas:
Organic, inorganic, analytical and physical chemistry, spectroscopy, environmental and green chemistry, natural products, polymers, materials, and applied chemical research.

Programme Philosophy & Objectives
What the Programme Aims to Develop

This is a student-friendly summary of the Chemistry programme's study areas, not a quotation of an official philosophy statement.

Programme Philosophy

To build a sound foundation in chemical principles and scientific reasoning, supported by practical laboratory skills, analysis, research and an understanding of how chemistry applies to materials, the environment and everyday life.

Learning Objectives

Develop a sound understanding of fundamental chemical principles.

Build competence in laboratory practice, observation, measurement and chemical analysis.

Understand chemical structures, reactions, kinetics and mechanisms.

Apply chemistry to environmental, material, industrial and other practical problems.

Develop research, data interpretation, communication and problem-solving skills.

Prepare students for further study and relevant scientific careers.

Programme Offered & Duration
Degree Programme

Industrial Chemistry has its own separate Uni Pilot page.

🎓

B.Sc. Industrial Chemistry

Undergraduate programme applying chemical principles to industrial processes, materials, production, quality control, laboratory practice and research.

⏱️

Normal Duration

UTME entry: 4 years (8 semesters). Direct Entry: 3 years (6 semesters), subject to the applicable university regulations.

🔬

Core Study Areas

Industrial processes, process science, petroleum and polymer chemistry, unit operations, catalysis, macromolecules, agrochemicals and chemical technology.

🧪

Practical Learning

Laboratory practicals, industrial attachments, seminar and research project work listed in the course structure.

Admission
Admission Requirements

Requirements transcribed from the supplied 2025/2026 Faculty Brochure. Applicants should confirm the current requirements with AAUA and JAMB.

UTME Entry Requirements

Five O’Level credit passes in not more than two sittings.

Required subjects: English Language, Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics, and Biology or Agricultural Science.

Normal programme duration: four years.

Direct Entry Requirements

A’Level passes in Chemistry and Physics or Mathematics; or

OND/HND Upper Credit in a relevant field, as stated in the supplied brochure.

Normal programme duration: three years.

Maximum Duration

The supplied brochure states a maximum of two additional sessions beyond the normal duration: up to 10 semesters for UTME entry and up to 8 semesters for Direct Entry.

WELCOME & BACKGROUND
About the Department

Based on the 2025/2026 Faculty Brochure.

Welcome to Industrial Mathematics at AAUA.
The Department of Mathematical Sciences offers Mathematics and Industrial Mathematics, with a commitment to excellence in teaching, research and applying mathematical knowledge to real-world challenges.

Programme overview:
Industrial Mathematics applies mathematical modelling, analysis and computational tools to problems in industry, finance and economics. It bridges theory and practice, helping graduates design efficient systems, optimise processes and support innovation in manufacturing, energy, logistics and technology.

Programme philosophy:
To prepare graduates for careers as mathematicians in business and industry, with strong technical ability to apply mathematical solutions to real-world problems.

Unique features:
The programme focuses on applying mathematics to industrial challenges, including financial and stock-related problems, while taking advantage of current technological innovations.

PROGRAMME INFORMATION
Objectives & Skills

Skills and objectives described in the 2025/2026 brochure.

Programme Objectives

Prepare students for demand in existing and emerging industrial sectors.

Develop enthusiasm for mathematics through a stimulating learning experience.

Provide a broad foundation in undergraduate mathematics and practical industrial applications.

Build the ability to apply mathematical knowledge to theoretical and practical problems.

Develop transferable skills and specialised skills in applied mathematics and multidisciplinary areas.

Employability & 21st-Century Skills

Creative and critical thinking, problem-solving, analytical thinking, initiative, quantitative reasoning, logical thinking, communication, time management, teamwork, independence, numeracy, computer and digital literacy, and the ability to work with precise and intricate ideas.

ENTRY & GRADUATION
Admission Requirements

Requirements transcribed from the supplied 2025/2026 brochure; confirm eligibility with AAUA Admissions.

UTME Entry · 100 Level

Five credit passes at not more than two sittings in SSCE or an equivalent qualification, including English Language, Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics and Biology/Agricultural Science or Economics. Candidates must pass UTME and the university screening.

UTME subjects:
English Language, Physics, Mathematics and Chemistry or Economics.

Direct Entry · 200 Level

Two relevant A-Level passes (graded A–E) through GCE/JUPEB in subjects such as Mathematics, Further Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry/Economics, or a good diploma with at least Upper Credit in Mathematics, Physics and Engineering.

Graduation Requirements

Pass all core courses, university/faculty/school required courses and electives. The brochure specifies a minimum of
120 course units for UTME students
and
90 course units for Direct Entry students
, alongside passing all required courses.

Introduction & General Background
Information and Communication Technology

It is with great pleasure and immense honor that I welcome you all to the Department of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) at Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko.

In the fast-evolving digital era, ICT plays a fundamental role in shaping the way we communicate, work, and interact with the world. Our department is committed to excellence in teaching, research, and industry collaboration, ensuring that our students are equipped with the knowledge and skills needed for the ICT field.

We take pride in our dynamic curriculum, state-of-the-art facilities, and dedicated faculty who are passionate about driving technological advancement. We foster an environment of creativity, critical thinking, and problem-solving to prepare future leaders, innovators, and professionals in the ICT field.

To our new students, welcome to a journey of learning and discovery. You are now part of a community that values knowledge, collaboration, and continuous growth. We encourage you to take advantage of the resources available, engage with your peers and mentors, and embrace challenges as opportunities for growth.

As we embark on this academic programme, let us remain steadfast in our pursuit of knowledge, innovation, and excellence. The future of ICT is bright, and with dedication and hard work, we can drive meaningful change and contribute to the ever-evolving digital landscape.

Dr. A. O. Akingbesote
HOD-ICT

General Overview:
Globally, there is a growing demand for Information and Communication Technology specialists to power and drive processes in business and non-business organisations. Information and Communication Technology has tremendous potential to boost operations efficiency, increase productivity and operate uninterruptedly with no downtime. The degree programme aims at producing ICT graduates with sufficient professional knowledge and skills to manage organisations' computing infrastructure and provide adequate support for computer users in order to enhance productivity and increase business value.

📍 View Department Location ↗

Programme Philosophy & Objectives
What the Programme Aims to Develop

Philosophy

The guiding principles of the programme is to equip Information and Communication Technology students with adequate skills and knowledge to provide seamless organisations' ICT integration for effective productivity and to support organisations' computer system users through best practices and professional standards.

Objectives

Provide students with a broad knowledge and practical skills in Information and Communication Technology.

Empower students to be problem-solvers through Information and Communication Technologies tools.

Equip students with the capacity for professional practice in the Information and Communication Technology sector.

Programme Offered & Duration
B.Sc. Information and Communication Technology

🎓

Bachelor of Science Degree in ICT

The programme offered is Bachelor of Science Degree in Information and Communication Technology.

⏱️

Duration

Candidates who enter through UTME normally spend 4 years (minimum), while Direct Entry candidates spend 3 years (minimum).

Admission
Admission Requirements

UTME Entry Requirements

Five O'Level credit passes at SSCE (WAEC, GCE, NECO and NABTEB) at not more than two sittings, including English Language and Mathematics, Physics, and two from Chemistry, Biology, Agricultural Science, Statistics, Additional Mathematics, Computer Studies, Studies, ICT or Basic Electronics.

UTME subjects must include Mathematics, Physics, and one of Biology, Chemistry, Agric Science, Economics, Geography or Computer Studies.

Candidates successful in the pre-degree programme (Science) of Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko can also be considered.

Direct Entry Requirements

Students coming into 200 level must satisfy one of the following:

Passes in two A'Level subjects which must include Mathematics, provided the O'Level requirement is satisfied.

At least Upper Credit Pass in ND Computer Science, Statistics or Electronics/Electrical Engineering, provided the O'Level requirement is satisfied.

NCE with at least Merit Pass in Computer Science, Mathematics or Statistics can also be considered, provided the O'Level requirement is satisfied.

Graduation
Graduation Requirements

Passed all core courses, university and faculty/school required courses and electives.

Accumulated a minimum of 146 course units for students admitted through UTME and 113 course units for students admitted to 200 level.

Attain a minimum CGPA of 1.00.

Be found worthy in character throughout the period of studentship and accumulate the total units prescribed for the programme from Core, Faculty and General Studies courses as well as SIWES, Seminar and Final Year Project.

Registration
Registration for Courses

Course Categories

Compulsory Courses:
Courses which students must offer and pass before graduation.

Elective Courses:
Departmental-prescribed courses required to be registered and passed to meet the minimum requirements of the University before graduation.

Registration Rules

The minimum work load is 15 units and the maximum is 28 units per semester.

A student can withdraw from a course within the time stipulated by Senate without penalty only with the approval of the HOD on completion of Add and Delete form.

Any student who withdraws without due permission will be deemed to have failed the course.

Any course examination sat for without registration will be cancelled.

18.2 · Programme Overview
Welcome to Information Systems

Department of Informatics and Information Systems, Adekunle Ajasin University.

It is with great pleasure and a deep sense of honor that I welcome you all to the Department of Informatics and Information Systems. Whether you are a new student embarking on an exciting academic journey, a returning student advancing your knowledge, or a faculty and staff member committed to shaping the future of this field, we are delighted to have you as part of our vibrant academic community.

In today's rapidly evolving digital world, Informatics and Information Systems play a crucial role in shaping industries, businesses, healthcare, security, education, and virtually every aspect of human life. Our department is dedicated to providing cutting-edge education, fostering innovative research, and preparing students to become leaders in the fields of information technology, data science, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, and more.

We take pride in our distinguished faculty, who are not only educators but also researchers and industry experts working on groundbreaking advancements in the field. Our state-of-the-art facilities, industry partnerships, and hands-on learning experiences ensure that our students are well-equipped with the knowledge and practical skills needed to excel in the ever-evolving tech landscape.

To our new students, you are embarking on a journey that will challenge you, inspire you, and equip you with the skills necessary to make meaningful contributions to society. We encourage you to take advantage of the various learning resources, research opportunities, and mentorship programs available within the department. To our returning students, we commend your dedication and perseverance, and we urge you to continue striving for excellence in your academic pursuits.

Collaboration and innovation are at the heart of what we do, and we invite all of you to actively engage in research initiatives, tech-driven projects, and knowledge-sharing platforms. The future belongs to those who can harness the power of information and technology to drive change, and we are committed to nurturing a community of thinkers, problem-solvers, and innovators.

As we embark on this new academic session, let us embrace the opportunities ahead with curiosity, determination, and a commitment to excellence. Together, we will push the boundaries of knowledge and contribute to the advancement of informatics and information systems.

Once again, welcome to the Department of Informatics and Information Systems. We look forward to an exciting and productive journey with you all!

Dr. S.O. Ogunlana

General Overview
Why Information Systems?

Information is a critical resource in driving all aspects of human endeavours, for optimal productivity and continuity for survival in a dynamic business environment. Information systems is the key enabler for running and managing processes in organisations today in a global economy. In the world today, entire sectors of economy rely heavily on information systems to thrive. Rational decision-making could only be made about business activities through a well-developed information system. The information system synopsis are aimed at producing information system specialists with adequate professional knowledge and skills to support organisation information needs to drive its core operations through adequate course work, practical and applied project experience.

Programme Philosophy & Objectives
What the Programme Aims to Develop

Programme Framework
Philosophy & Objectives

Programme Philosophy

The philosophy of the programme is to equip Information Systems graduates with sufficient knowledge and skills to collect, process, store, distribute information and to use information systems to support decision making, control and coordination in an organisation for increased productivity through best practices and professional standards.

Programme Objectives

Create the consciousness of the relevance of information systems as a primary driver in all economic sectors.

Equip students with appropriate skills and knowledge to develop and manage information system resources in an organisation.

Empower students with problem-solving skills.

Develop students with the ability to use information systems to improve business operations.

Develop students with capacity to manage various information systems in an organisation to best serve the people (manager, staff and customers).

Equip students with demonstrable business knowledge and applications of software proficiency.

Equip students with capacity for professional practice in information systems and communication.

UTME Entry Requirements

Five O'Level credit passes at SSCE (WAEC, GCE, NECO, and NABTEB) at no more than two sittings, including English Language, Mathematics, Physics, and two from Chemistry, Biology/Agric Science, Statistics, Additional Mathematics, Computer Studies, ICT, or Basic Electronics.

UTME subjects must include Use of English, Mathematics, Physics, and one of Biology, Chemistry, Agric Science, Economics, Geography, and Computer Studies.

Candidates successful in the pre-degree programme (Science) of Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko can also be considered.

Direct Entry Requirements

Students entering 200 Level must satisfy one of the following, provided the O'Level requirement in 18.4(a) is satisfied:

Passes in two A' Level subjects, which must include Mathematics.

At least Upper Credit in ND Computer Science, Statistics, or Electronics/Electrical Engineering.

NCE with at least Merit in Computer Science, Mathematics, or Statistics.

Minimum duration:
4 sessions for UTME and 3 sessions for candidates admitted to 200 Level.

Attain a minimum CGPA of 1.00.

Be found worthy in character throughout the period of studentship.

Accumulate the prescribed units from Core, Faculty, General Studies courses, SIWES, Seminar, and Final Year Project.

WELCOME & BACKGROUND
About the Department

Programme overview, philosophy and academic purpose from the 2025/2026 Faculty Brochure.

Programme overview:
The B.Sc. Mathematics programme equips students with a solid foundation in mathematical theory, analytical reasoning and problem-solving. It builds confidence and independence in addressing diverse challenges, helping graduates apply mathematical knowledge in academic, professional and real-world settings.

Philosophy:
The programme aims to develop academic excellence and competence in mathematical reasoning and problem-solving through logic and computational skills. It is also intended to help meet national needs in technological advancement, a continuing global priority.

Programme context:
Mathematics and Industrial Mathematics are offered within the Department of Mathematical Sciences. Uni Pilot keeps their guides separate so students can quickly find the correct programme information.

LEARNING & DEVELOPMENT
Programme Objectives & Employability Skills

Programme Objectives

Build enthusiasm for mathematics and appreciation of its applications in different areas.

Provide a broad, balanced foundation in mathematical knowledge and practical skills in statistics and computer science.

Develop the ability to apply mathematical knowledge to theoretical and practical problems.

Build transferable skills useful in mathematics-related and other employment.

Prepare students for advanced study in specialised or multidisciplinary areas involving mathematics.

Develop appreciation of mathematics in industrial, economic, environmental and social contexts.

Employability Skills

Learning and innovation skills.

Life and career skills.

Information, media and technology skills.

Quantitative reasoning.

Ability to manipulate precise and intricate ideas.

Numeracy and logical problem-solving.

PROGRAMME OFFERED & DURATION
Degree Programme

Programme details from the supplied 2025/2026 Faculty Brochure.

∑

B.Sc. Mathematics

Study mathematical theory, logic, analysis, algebra, statistics, numerical methods, modelling and computational approaches to problem-solving.

⏳

Normal Duration

Typically 4 years for UTME entry and 3 years for Direct Entry, subject to the university's current regulations.

ENTRY & GRADUATION
Admission Requirements

Requirements reproduced from the supplied 2025/2026 Faculty Brochure.

Indirect Entry · 100 Level

At least credit-level passes in five subjects at SSC/O’Level or equivalent, including English Language, Mathematics and Physics, plus credits in any two of Chemistry, Biology or Agricultural Science. An acceptable UTME result with the appropriate subject combination is also required.

Direct Entry · 200 Level

Two relevant GCE/IJMB Advanced Level passes (grades A–E) in subjects such as Mathematics, Further Mathematics, Physics or Chemistry; or a good diploma with at least Upper Credit in Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science and Engineering, as stated in the brochure.

Graduation Requirements

The brochure states a minimum of
120 credits for UTME students
and
90 credits for Direct Entry students
. Confirm the requirement that applies to your cohort with the department.

Introduction & General Background
Department of Pure and Applied Psychology

**Programme offered:** Bachelor of Science (B.Sc.) Psychology.

Psychology is a scientific discipline which studies human and non-human behaviours from the physiological roots to the social influence processes which equips the students with skills needed for the explanation, prediction and modification of those behaviours for lasting peace and order in human society.

As a profession in the social sciences, psychology aims to provide students with a top-ranked undergraduate education in various areas of psychology which include but are not limited to Clinical psychology, Neurobiological psychology, Behavioural medicine/Medical psychology, Social psychology, Industrial/organisational psychology, Positive psychology, health psychology among others.

The goal of the programme is to train the next generation of leaders, innovators, and cutting-edge professionals in these diverse areas of psychology with the needed 21st-century skills. Graduates of Psychology are well-equipped for job opportunities in Health institutions, Schools, NGOs, Self-employment, industries, and security agencies.

Programme Philosophy
Philosophy of the Programme

As a science, Psychology seeks to discover patterns of behaviour, using facts, principles and generalizations, in order to increase our knowledge and understanding of individual behaviour in various social and cultural settings, groups, institutions and organizations for proper adaptation or adjustment and development.

The philosophy behind the Psychology curriculum in Nigerian Universities is therefore to equip students with skills, concepts and principles which can help them to understand, explain, predict, modify, and change human and non-human behaviours for intra- and interpersonal harmonious coexistence and overall social, economic, political, and national development of Nigeria.

Admission
Admission Requirements

Four-year programme

In addition to UTME score, the candidate should possess at least five O’Level credit passes, including Mathematics, English Language, Biology, and any other two subjects from Social Sciences, Arts or Sciences or its equivalent at not more than two sittings.

Three-year programme

In addition to having five O’Level credits passes in English Language, Mathematics, Biology and two other subjects, Direct Entry candidates must have at least three Advanced Level or Joint Universities Preliminary Examination Board (JUPEB) credits passes, which must include English Language, Mathematics and Biology. He/she must have at least a total grade point of 6.0.

Candidates with relevant National Diploma (ND) with at least upper credit, Nursing and Midwifery certificates as well as Diploma in Psychology (at least Upper Credit), from any institution recognized by the Senate of this University, are also qualified, provided such candidates have credit passes in the relevant O’Level subjects.

Direct Entry note:
All Direct Entry students would be required to take and pass designated courses at the 100 Level.

About the Faculty

Welcome to the Faculty of Science at Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko, a vibrant academic community where scientific excellence meets societal relevance.

The Faculty is committed to rigorous scientific education, impactful research, innovation, and the development of students who can contribute meaningfully to society. Through its diverse programmes, practical learning, and research activities, students are prepared for careers and lifelong contributions to science and humanity.

We welcome newly admitted and returning students to pursue academic excellence with diligence, integrity, critical thinking, and a strong sense of responsibility. The Faculty also welcomes alumni, industry partners, government agencies, NGOs, and other stakeholders to support research, mentorship, innovation, and opportunities for students.

The Faculty of Science is a community of learning, research, and innovation. Explore its departments, discover its programmes, and connect with the opportunities available within the Faculty.

19.2 · Introduction & General Background
Software Engineering

It is with great pleasure and enthusiasm that I welcome you all to the Department of Software Engineering. Whether you are a new student embarking on your academic journey, a returning scholar, or a respected faculty member, we are honored to have you as part of our dynamic and innovative community.

Software Engineering is at the heart of modern technological advancements, driving solutions across industries such as finance, healthcare, education, and artificial intelligence. In this department, we are committed to equipping our students with the technical knowledge, problem-solving skills, and hands-on experience needed to thrive in an ever-evolving digital world.

Our distinguished faculty, cutting-edge research initiatives, and strong industry collaborations provide a solid foundation for learning, creativity, and professional growth. We encourage students to embrace innovation, engage in collaborative projects, and develop solutions that address real-world challenges.

As we embark on another academic session, I urge you to take full advantage of the resources available, participate in workshops and hackathons, and contribute to groundbreaking research in Software Engineering. The future belongs to those who are willing to learn, adapt, and create.

Once again, welcome to the Department of Software Engineering. Together, let us code, innovate, and build a smarter tomorrow!

Thank you.
Dr Mrs E.O Aliyu

📍 View Department Location ↗

The software development industry presents huge opportunities within the context of an expanding global economy that is increasingly becoming digital. With the enormous potentials of this sector of the economy and the ever increasing need for large and complex software systems, there is great promise to grow a large crop of software engineers as a force for sustainable socio-economic development. In addition to its core Computer Science foundation, Software Engineering also involves human and technical processes, and therefore borrows and adapts from the field of project management as well as from traditional engineering practice.

Programme Objectives
What the Programme Aims to Develop

Philosophy

The philosophy of Software Engineering focuses on producing graduates who have the required knowledge and skills to develop and maintain quality software systems of scale for governments, organisations and businesses that adequately fulfil the functional and nonfunctional requirements of the systems within time and budget constraints.

Objectives

Provide a solid foundation in computing, including problem solving, algorithm design, data structures and programming basics.

Demonstrate practical skills in requirements analysis, system design, software architecture, software metrics, verification and validation, and the software engineering process in general for the production of high quality software-based systems.

Demonstrate expertise in programming in different languages, with emphasis on robust, reliable, cost-effective and secure systems based on sound design and development principles.

Train students to effectively and efficiently manage the development of large, complex and critical software.

Enable students to acquire the requisite knowledge and skills, practical exposure and high ethical standards for professional career opportunities, including self-employment, in the software industry.

Degree Programme
B.Sc. Software Engineering

🎓

Bachelor of Science Degree in Software Engineering

The programme offered is a Bachelor of Science Degree in Software Engineering. The prospectus gives a minimum duration of four years for UTME candidates and three years for Direct Entry candidates.

⏳

Programme Duration

UTME: 4 years minimum. Direct Entry: 3 years minimum.

Admission Requirements
Admission Requirements

UTME Entry Requirements

Five O'Level credit passes at SSCE (WAEC, GCE, NECO and NABTEB) in not more than two sittings, including English Language, Mathematics and Physics, plus two from Chemistry, Biology/Agric Science, Statistics, Additional Mathematics, Computer Studies, ICT or Basic Electronics.

UTME subjects must include Use of English, Mathematics, Physics, and one of Biology, Chemistry, Agric Science, Economics, Geography or Computer Studies.

Candidates successful in the pre-degree programme (Science) of Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko can also be considered.

Direct Entry Requirements

Students entering 200 level must satisfy one of the following, provided the O'Level requirements above are met:

Passes in two A'Level subjects, which must include Mathematics.

At least Upper Credit in ND Computer Science, Statistics or Electronics/Electrical Engineering.

NCE with at least Merit in Computer Science, Mathematics or Statistics.

Graduation Requirements
Graduation Requirements

Pass all core courses, university and faculty/school-required courses and electives.

Accumulate a minimum of 153 course units for students admitted through UTME and 121 course units for students admitted to 200 level, as stated in the prospectus.

Attain a minimum CGPA of 1.00.

To graduate, a student must be found worthy in character throughout the period of study and accumulate the total units prescribed for the programme from Core, Faculty, General Studies courses, SIWES, Seminar and Final Year project.

Source note:
The graduation paragraph in the supplied prospectus mistakenly names Data Science. The department context and programme heading identify this section as Software Engineering, so the department name has been aligned. The 3-year unit total is inconsistent elsewhere in the prospectus and is flagged in the programme summary below.

Course Registration
Registration for Courses

Candidates must register for appropriate compulsory and elective courses as indicated in the prospectus.

Compulsory courses:
Courses students must offer and pass before graduation.

Elective courses:
Department-prescribed courses required to be registered and passed to meet the University's minimum requirements before graduation.

The minimum workload is 15 units and the maximum is 28 units per semester.

A student may withdraw from a course within the Senate-stipulated period without penalty only with HOD approval and completion of an Add and Delete form. Withdrawal without permission is deemed a failed course.

Any course examination sat for without registration will be cancelled.
